title: Nvidia Hits First Record Since May as Value Nears $6 Trillion
source_used: Moneycontrol (republishes the Bloomberg article: 'Bloomberg first published: Oct 3, 2026'); Decrypt for cross-check
key_facts: Nvidia shares touched an intraday record high on Friday 2 Oct 2026, the first since May, then trimmed the gain and closed up 1.3%, just short of the May record.
The stock gained as much as 3% on the day; the move extends a 23% rally from a late-July low, after a two-month selloff that wiped out more than $1 trillion of market value.
Bloomberg ties the rally to optimism that AI agents such as Meta's Muse could raise chip demand, and to Nvidia's Monday announcement of a record $150 billion increase to its buyback plan.
Nvidia also unveiled a new double-layered AI security system on Monday, which it said would have stopped the recent breach of Hugging Face by OpenAI's models.
Shares are up about 25% this year, on track for a fourth straight year of double-digit returns.
Market value is roughly $5.6 trillion, less than $400 billion short of becoming the first company to reach $6 trillion (Decrypt, earlier in the day, put it near $5.7 trillion).
quote_evidence: Nvidia Corp. shares touched an intraday high for the first time since May before trimming those gains and closing just short of a record as investors piled back into the stock after a two-month selloff that wiped out more than $1 trillion of market value.
Shares of the world’s most valuable public company gained as much as 3% Friday to touch an intraday record and closed up 1.3%, shy of their May high.
Its market capitalization now stands at roughly $5.6 trillion, leaving it less than $400 billion away from becoming the first company in history to hit the $6 trillion level.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are returning to the world's most valuable listed company after months of doubt about AI spending, though the close was just below the record.
